questions.q:
The charge accumulated on the capacitor connected in the following circuit is ______μC.

(Given C=150 μF)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Under the balanced condition, the capacitor will act as an open circuit.

The current i1 through the 1 Ω resistor is given by

i1=10 V1 Ω+2 Ω=103 A

The current i2 through the 6 Ω resistor is given by

i2=10 V6 Ω+4 Ω=1 A

From the above diagram, it can be written that

VA+i1×1-i2×6=VB⇒VA-VB=1×6-103×1=83 V

Hence, the charge on the capacitor is given by

Q=CVA-VB=150 μF×83 V=400 μC

The change in the electrostatic energy in the capacitor will be __________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initially
C=200μF
Ei=12CV2=12×200×10-6×2002
Finally
C'=KC=400μF
Ef=12C'V2=12×400×10-6×(200)2
ΔE=12×400-200×10-6×4×104=4 J

questions.q: A time varying potential difference is applied between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $2.5 \mu \mathrm{~F}$. The dielectric constant of the medium between the capacitor plates is 1 . It produces an instantaneous displacement current of 0.25 mA in the intervening space between the capacitor plates, the magnitude of the rate of change of the potential difference will be _____ $\mathrm{Vs}^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{CdV}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}}{\mathrm{C}} \\ & =\frac{0.25 \times 10^{-3}}{2.5 \times 10^{-6}} \\ & =100\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A parallel plate capacitor with plate area A and plate separation d is filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constant K=4. The thickness of the dielectric material is x, where x<d.

Let C1 and C2 be the capacitance of the system for x=13d and x=2d3, respectively. If C1=2 μF, the value of C2 is _____ μF.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor having thickness d and with a dielectric of thickness x between the plates is given by

C=ε0Ad-x+xK   ...(1)

Substitute the values of the parameters for first case into equation (1) to obtain the capacitance.

C1=ε0A2d3+d34=4ε0A3d   ...(2)

Similarly, substitute the parameters into equation (1) for the second case to obtain the capacitance

C2=ε0Ad3+2d34=4ε0A2d=2ε0Ad   ...(3)

Divide equation (3) by equation (2) to obtain the capacitance in the second case.

C2C1=2ε0Ad4ε0A3d= 32C2=32C1   ...(4)

Substitute the value of the capacitance in the first case into equation (4) to obtain the value of the capacitance in the second case.

C2=32×2 μF= 3 μF

questions.q:
The electric field between the two parallel plates of a capacitor of $1.5 \mu \mathrm{F}$ capacitance drops to one third of its initial value in $6.6 \mu \mathrm{s}$ when the plates are connected by a thin wire.
The resistance of this wire is _____$\Omega$. (Given, $\log 3=1.1$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}=\frac{\mathrm{E}_0}{3} \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_0}{3} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{V}_0}{3}=\mathrm{V}_0 \mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{t}}{\tau}} \\ & \mathrm{t}=\tau \ell \mathrm{n} 3 \\ & 6.6 \times 10^{-6}=\mathrm{R}\left(1.5 \times 10^{-6}\right)(1.1) \\ & \mathrm{R}=\frac{6}{1.5}=4 \Omega\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A composite parallel plate capacitor is made up of two different dielectric materials with different thickness (t1 and t2) as shown in figure. The two different dielectric material are separated by a conducting foil F. The voltage of the conducting foil is _____ V.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Capacitance of each capacitor 

C1=A3ε012=6 Aϵ0 and C2=A4ϵ01=4Aε0

Here, A is area of plate.

Equivalent capacitance is 

Ceq=C1C2C1+C2=6Aε0×4Aε06Aε0+4Aε0=2410Aϵ0

Now, net charge stored is qnet=CeqΔV=2410Aε0100=240Aε0

Potential drop across C2 is ΔV2=240Aε04Aε0=60 V

Thus, voltage of the conducting foil is Vfoil =60 V

questions.q:
Two parallel plate capacitors C1 and C2 each having capacitance of 10 μF are individually charged by a 100 V D.C. source. Capacitor C1 is kept connected to the source and a dielectric slab is inserted between it plates. Capacitor C2 is disconnected from the source and then a dielectric slab is inserted in it. Afterwards the capacitor C1 is also disconnected from the source and the two capacitors are finally connected in parallel combination. The common potential of the combination will be _____ V.

(Assuming Dielectric constant =10)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As source is connected in the process therefore, additional charge will be provided. Therefore, charge on C1=KCV.

Since source is disconnected, so its charge will remain the same. Then, charge on C2=CV.

New capacitance in both cases will become, KC.

When they are connected in parallel charge will be equally divided so charge on one capacitor is q=K+12CV.

So common potential,

V'=qKC=K+12KV=55 V.

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> and potential <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> has energy <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo>.</mo></math> It is connected to another capacitor of capacitance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>C</mi></math> and potential <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>V</mi></math>. Then the loss of energy is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>E</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, E=12CV2

Required energy loss 

=12C1C2C1+C2V1-V22=12C×2CC+2CV-2V2

=26CV2=23·E

∴x=2

questions.q: Space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of plate area $4 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ and separation of (d) 1.77 mm, is filled with uniform dielectric materials with dielectric constants (3 and 5) as shown in figure. Another capacitor of capacitance 7.5 pF is connected in parallel with it. The effective capacitance of this combination is ________ pF. $\left(\right.$ Given $\left.\varepsilon_0=8.85 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~F} / \mathrm{m}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{C}_1=\frac{5 \times 4 \times 10^{-4} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}}{\frac{1.77}{2} \times 10^{-3}}=20 \mathrm{pF} \\ & \mathrm{C}_2=\frac{3 \times 4 \times 10^{-4} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}}{\frac{1.77}{2} \times 10^{-3}}=12 \mathrm{pF} \\ & \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{C}_2}{\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2}=\frac{12 \times 20}{12+20}=7.5 \mathrm{pF}\end{aligned}$
Finally equivalent capacitance
$\left(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{eq}}\right)_{\text {final }}=7.5+7.5=15 \mathrm{pF}$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor with air between the plate has a capacitance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi>pF</mi></math>. The separation between the plate becomes twice and the space between them is filled with a medium of dielectric constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Capacitance of the parallel plate capacitor when air is present between the plates, C=ε0Ad=15 pF

Capacitance of the parallel plate capacitor when dielectric is filled in between the plates,

 C'=kε0Ad'=3.5ε0A2d=3.52×15 pF=1054 pF

Therefore, x=105.

=1008 pJ
